newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Copper prices hit OrienMet net -analysts.
newsitem.headline: Copper prices hit OrienMet net -analysts.

text.p: Metals trading firm Oriental Metals' (OrienMet) 99 percent plunge in 1996 net profit largely reflected a slide in copper prices, analysts said on Wednesday.
"The market price of copper decreased in 1996 and so the value of their stocks purchased earlier was higher than the subsequent value of products," one analyst said.
On Tuesday, OrienMet posted turnover of HK$3.02 billion and a net profit of HK$1.28 million for the 12 months to December 31, 1996, a drop of one percent and 99 percent respectively.
The company suffered an exceptional loss of HK$36 million from the sale of its entire interest in Jinhui Holdings Co Ltd, the results announcement said.
OrienMet is authorised by the state-owned China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp to engage in trading nonferrous metals.

The company statement said copper price movements in China in 1996 generally reflected international patterns, but briefly sank under a large influx of imports before being rescued by firmer world prices.

One analyst said trading had not been badly affected because actual copper trading had risen in the period, adding however that the poor performance of industrial investments in copper and aluminium largely contributed to plummeting profits.
The firm's results statement said trade turnover for copper products, including cathodes, concentrates and blisters, grew by 19 percent over 1995.

"Plagued by falling international prices for nonferrous metals, particularly copper and aluminium, OrienMet's industrial investment projects in the People's Republic of China performed unsatisfactorily," the statement added.
